tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP is selected for its ability to provide consistent, interpretable, and per-feature importance scores across the dataset, especially in tabular models like TabNN. By applying it to all misclassified instances and focusing on the intersection of high importance features, we can detect spurious signals that dominate predictions despite lacking semantic relevance. Sensitivity analysis complements this by quantifying how much prediction changes when each feature is removed, helping to isolate features that drive misclassification even when the value is not meaningful. The combination enables robust detection of shared spurious features that are both present and influential.

LIME offers local interpretability to validate whether high attribution is consistent for individual predictions. Integrated Gradients offer gradient-based attribution useful in detecting subtle, spurious patterns.
